# Syncranicity: month-end option shortlist
Research date: October 29, 2026. Decision deadline: October 31, 2026.

**First choice: Hinds 110 near Vernon, Texas.** It remains the most sensible place to concentrate the next two days because the advertised land basis is low, the tract is large, and your October 28 AEP conversation creates a concrete next diligence step. This is a priority for conditional control negotiations. No reviewed property currently clears the evidence needed to recommend a nonrefundable option payment.

The ranking reflects your low-capital, control-first strategy for a roughly 20–30 MW project within a broader 10–50 MW lane. It is an analyst judgment about what to pursue next, not a measured probability of assignment profit. Seller willingness to grant an option, option prices, assignment rights, and buyer takeout have not been confirmed.

## Ranked candidates

| Priority | Property and direct listing | Advertised land price / contemplated scope | Why pursue it | What must change before paid control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Hinds 110 — Wilbarger County, TX](https://www.land.com/property/110-acres-in-wilbarger-county-texas/27899900/) | $319,500 for about 110 acres; MLS syndication shows $319,000 | Lowest whole-tract price among the leading candidates; FM 2072 frontage and advertised transmission crossings | Exact parcel and seller authority; serving utility and delivery point; written response for the actual load, upgrade costs and timing; usable footprint after easements; fiber route and viable assignment terms |
| 2 | [Sherrill / former Georgia-Pacific property — Chiefland, FL](https://www.loopnet.com/Listing/13550-NW-Old-Fannin-Rd-Chiefland-FL/39339766/) | $7 million whole property, approximately 352 acres; pursue a roughly 40-acre split only. $800,000 is illustrative at the advertised $20,000/acre, not a subdivision quote | Most useful published technical study in this shortlist; an identifiable utility upgrade path to investigate | Written split price and boundary retaining necessary utility/access rights; current Duke response; funded diligence and extension runway; environmental, water and fiber review |
| 3 | [Great Lakes Tech Park — 705 N Graham Road, Thomas Township / Saginaw, MI](https://properties.zoomprospector.com/michigan/property/705-N-Graham-Rd-Thomas-Twp.-Michigan/8FC7960D-2B8D-4721-BFF9-8F0FFDB750C3) | $24,000/acre; 20–30 acres implies $480,000–$720,000 before any special terms | Established park, a divisible offering, utility and fiber designations | Consumers Energy must quantify capacity; local authority must confirm data-center use; public owner must allow timely option/assignment; old studies need refresh |
| 4 | [N State Road 3 — New Castle, IN](https://www.land.com/property/44.35-acres-in-henry-county-indiana/27254380/) | $899,900 for 44.35 acres | Private-market backup with highway access and advertised nearby substation | Actual available MW, electric provider, route/cost/schedule, fiber, zoning and option economics |
| 5 | [48th Street NW / Highway 1804 — Williston, ND](https://www.commercialcafe.com/commercial-property/us/nd/williston/heavy-industrial-lots-from-10-acres-19-900-acre-next-to-substation-terminal/) | $19,900/acre; advertised lots from 10 acres. A 20–30-acre example is $398,000–$597,000 | Smaller industrial parcels may permit inexpensive control | Utility engineer must replace the listing's capacity placeholder with evidence; carrier routes, neighboring hazards, buyer fit and exact sale parcel must be resolved |

Prices above are land purchase asks or explicitly labeled arithmetic. They are not option premiums, appraisals, or seller-accepted terms.

### 1. Hinds: best near-term negotiation target

The listing describes 138 kV and 345 kV lines crossing cultivated land, with rural water and electricity available. None establishes a right to connect a 20–30 MW load. The $500 asking-price discrepancy is minor, but the seller must reconcile it.

Your AEP call advances access to information; it does not establish capacity or the serving utility. Obtain the county parcel identifier and boundary before treating a broker map pin as the project site. The website property number 27899900 is a listing ID, not a county parcel number.

The value-creation thesis is to secure transferable control at an ordinary land basis, then develop a credible, transferable utility and site package that a qualified developer will pay for. That exit remains unproven.

[Alternate MLS listing](https://www.briggsfreeman.com/property/tbd-county-road-105-n-vernon-tx-76384/106546019/)

### 2. Chiefland: strongest technical lead, longer runway

The June 2025 Duke-sponsored Site Readiness report estimates 25–36 months and equipment upgrades for 10 MW. For 20+ MW it identifies a substation rebuild and additional transformer; costs were not evaluated. The report also flags additional site diligence, water/sewer work and adjacent fiber. These are preliminary findings, not a current power reservation. The passage of time since publication does not shorten an unstarted upgrade schedule.

The offering memorandum allows 40-acre subdivisions. Require the selected tract to include enforceable access to the necessary electric, fiber, road and water corridors. The whole $7 million offering is a poor fit for your present capital model. A small, correctly located split could be worth pursuing if its control period reaches a realistic, funded monetization milestone.

[Broker listing](https://totalcommercial.com/listings/e1c95cd4-3116-4a70-bd74-5c8a168c7f72?where%5Buser.id%5D=23136) · [Offering memorandum](https://totalcommercial.com/attachment/131332/Offering%20Memorandum%20Levy%20County%20Property%20350%20Acre%20OM%20Branded%2013550%20NW%20Old%20Fannin%20Rd%20Chiefland%20FL.pdf) · [Technical report, especially PDF page 20](https://totalcommercial.com/media/273917/Duke-Energy-Site-Readiness---Levy---Sherrill-Property-Report---6.26.2025.pdf)

Chiefland already appeared in the October 27 watch ledger. The deeper study review is new work in this run; the listing itself is not newly discovered.

### 3. Saginaw: organized offering, uncertain control and power

The official listing advertises 114 acres, divisions of at least 10 acres, AT&T Fiber Ready and Consumers Energy Energy Ready designations. It provides no committed MW. The owner is the Economic Development Corporation of Saginaw County; diligence dates run back to 2009–2011. Verify which acreage and terms are current.

Public ownership may complicate a two-day option transaction and an eventual assignment. Ask whether an intermediary can acquire transferable control and what development obligations attach. A developer's ability to deal directly with the public owner also limits the value of a generic information package.

### 4–5. New Castle and Williston: keep as backups

New Castle's MLS listing remained active in the retrieved page, last updated October 8. Nearby electrical equipment and high-pressure gas are useful leads; the listing supplies no engineering evidence of deliverable power.

Williston's September 29 listing contains the literal phrase “X MW available.” Treat capacity as unknown. Its description also places it among oil storage and pipeline infrastructure. Independent separation, environmental, insurance and buyer-fit review would be necessary. Its affordability does not yet compensate for those gaps.

## Other properties reviewed: links and disposition

Price undisclosed. Broker brochure describes staged substation expansion; obtain current utility evidence and seller availability before ranking it above active leads. |
| Benson, AZ, parcel 120-02-003A | [Hartmann broker offering, first property on page](https://hcreinc.com/land) | Broker advertises 90 acres at $550,000 and RU-4 zoning; older marketing differs. Exact offered acreage, data-center land use and load capacity unresolved. Hold. |

| Dillon-Baker Compartment 1, Dillon County, SC | [51.60-acre AFM listing](https://www.afmrealestate.com/properties/51.6-acres-land-for-sale-in-dillon-county-south-carolina/dillon-baker-compartment-1) | $608,880 offering reviewed. No demonstrated data-center load or carrier path. Do not conflate this tract with an earlier, separately referenced Dillon port candidate. |
| 2900 24th Avenue North, Birmingham, AL | [11-acre, $750,000 listing](https://www.ratemyagent.com/real-estate-agency/keller-williams-realty-vestavi/property-listings/2900-24th-avenue-north-birmingham-bqphc2) | Heavy-industrial marketing and an existing tenant do not establish power or a clean development pad. No promotion over Hinds. |
| 000 Allied Way, Little Rock, AR | [Property status page](https://www.homes.com/property/000-allied-way-little-rock-ar/nf3sc74hnvbek/) | Prior $563,250 / 22.53-acre lead; this page now says not listed for sale. Treat availability as unresolved; do not carry an old active label forward. |
| 9596 Johnson Road, Phelan, CA | [9.73-acre listing](https://www.cityfeet.com/cont/listing/9596-johnson-rd-phelan-ca-92371/cs40310175) | $1.3 million ask; power claims remain conditional and the footprint is small. Weak fit for present capital/deadline. |
| 41685 20th Street W, Palmdale, CA | [9.77-acre listing](https://www.cityfeet.com/cont/listing/41685-20th-st-w-palmdale-ca-93551/cs40371627) | Current marketing shows $595,000. Battery/export-oriented electrical claims do not establish data-center import rights. Hold. |
| 416½ W Donlon Street, Blythe, CA | [6.05-acre offering](https://www.loopnet.com/Listing/416-1-2-W-Donlon-St-Blythe-CA/40340908/) | Small BESS-oriented opportunity; no demonstrated data-center import capacity. Exclude from deadline shortlist. |
| Dorth Place, Twentynine Palms, CA | [10-acre offering](https://www.loopnet.com/Listing/Dorth-Pl-Twentynine-Palms-CA/40294899/) | Battery-oriented marketing and unresolved land-use path. Exclude from deadline shortlist. |

This is a focused refresh of leading candidates and new comparables, not a fresh qualification of every property in the national atlas. Advertised status was checked through public pages; no owner or utility independently confirmed availability during this run.

## What I would do by the deadline

1. **October 29: concentrate on Hinds.** Request current seller availability, exact legal description/APNs, title/easement materials, price and a written proposal for assignable control. Give the utility the exact site and honest phased load profile, including total facility demand rather than IT load alone. Identify the serving provider, transmission owner, delivery point and applicable process.
2. **October 30: require decision-useful evidence.** Seek a dated utility response describing whether the proposed load can be studied, indicative upgrades/timing, initial study charges and security requirements. Get a carrier route/build-cost indication and a preliminary use/footprint screen. In parallel, ask Chiefland for a 40-acre split proposal and updated utility study assumptions.
3. **October 31: sign only an instrument that fits the evidence and cash runway.** If key issues remain open, use a counsel-drafted conditional/refundable structure or continue unpaid diligence. Do not convert the calendar deadline into a reason to accept uncontrolled downside.

Friday, October 30 is the practical business-response deadline ahead of Saturday, October 31.

## Negotiating targets for a Hinds option

These are proposed terms for counsel and negotiation, not a seller quote or a conclusion about enforceability:

- Start with a 60–90 day diligence period and $0–$2,000 initial cash exposure, with refund/termination protection for agreed power, title and land-use failures.
- Fix the purchase basis and exact property; retain assignment rights, access for noninvasive diligence and rights to share/transfer reports to a qualified acquirer.
- Secure enforceable extension choices with predetermined prices. Test whether approximately 12–18 months reaches the specific assignment milestone; extend that runway only if costs and a funding source are credible.
- Keep the initial learning budget within $5,000 and total cumulative soft-control exposure on one parcel within your $10,000 cap, including legal, studies, option consideration and extensions.
- Retain enough capital to produce the evidence a buyer would purchase. Identify named, independent prospective acquirers and their requirements, the monetization milestone and the funded path to it before nonrefundable exposure.
- Stop if the seller requires a large nonrefundable premium, prohibits assignment, cannot give reliable access, or gives a control period shorter than the funded diligence path.

No modeled assignment profit, resale premium or success percentage is supportable from the available inputs. A credible option thesis still requires a buyer who values the specific deliverable, not just general industry demand.

## Additional source and policy notes

[Rocky Mountain Power large-service requirements](https://www.rockymountainpower.net/working-with-us/large-service-requests.html) describe a $150,000 minimum initial evaluation charge for the 25–199 MW tier. This makes a self-funded Evanston route difficult under your present cap. A smaller project has a different process; it does not follow that utility studies are free.

For a Texas site, first establish whether ERCOT rules apply. [ERCOT's September 14 medium-load notice](https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/M-B091426-01) addresses substantiated loads from 25 MW to below 75 MW. Do not choose or describe an artificially smaller load to avoid the applicable process.

Ranking was informed by your Selection Factors, Probability and Stop Gates, and control-first research guidance. No funds were committed and no outside messages were sent.
